issues.legal_issue: A grantee who accepts a government-confirmed land grant subject to a condition against evicting tenants is bound by that condition.
material_facts: A ruler had granted agricultural land to the grantee, and the successor government questioned the grant.
The government confirmed the grant subject to a condition that the grantee would not evict the cultivators.
Although not a party to the government’s arrangement with the ruler, the grantee knew of and accepted the grant on those conditions.
issues.conclusion: The grantee was bound by the condition against evicting the tenants.
issues.legal_principle: The government could have annulled the grant, in which case the annulment would have been an Act of State that could not be questioned before municipal tribunals. Instead, it confirmed the grant subject to conditions that the grantee accepted, and the grantee was bound by them. The Court relied on State of Saurashtra v. Jamadar Mohamad Abdulla, [1962] 3 S.C.R. 970.

predicates.conditional_grant_dispute: The dispute concerns a land grant confirmed by a successor government subject to a condition.
predicates.government_confirmed_grant_with_conditio: The government confirmed the grant on the condition that the grantee would not evict the cultivators.
predicates.grantee_accepted_condition: The grantee knew of and accepted the grant subject to that condition.
predicates.grantee_bound_by_accepted_condition: The grantee is bound by the accepted condition.

issues.definition: When a dispute concerns a condition attached to a government-confirmed grant, and the grantee accepted that condition, the grantee is bound by it.

issues.legal_issue: A tenant’s protection against eviction arising from a condition attached to a grant is a right or privilege arising out of a grant and is preserved by the land-reform legislation.
material_facts: The government confirmed the grant subject to a condition that the grantee would not evict the cultivators.
The condition was intended to benefit the tenants and was attached to the grant to the grantee.
The legislation preserved tenants’ rights and privileges arising from grants.
issues.conclusion: The tenants could rely on the non-eviction condition as a right or privilege arising out of a grant, and the legislation did not limit or abridge it.
issues.legal_principle: Section 18 of the Saurashtra Land Reforms Act, 1951, provides that the Act does not limit or abridge a tenant’s rights or privileges arising from a grant. The word “grant” in section 18 includes a government grant to a Girasdar; it is not limited to a grant made by a Girasdar to a tenant.

predicates.tenant_rights_dispute: The dispute concerns tenants’ protection against eviction from land held under a grant.
predicates.grant_condition_protects_tenants_from_ev: The grant was subject to a condition that the grantee would not evict the tenants.
predicates.condition_attached_to_land_grant: The non-eviction condition was attached to the grant of the land.
predicates.tenant_condition_is_protected_grant_priv: The tenants’ protection under the condition is a grant-based privilege that the legislation does not abridge.

issues.definition: When a grant’s condition protects tenants from eviction, that protection is preserved as a privilege arising from the grant.

issues.legal_issue: A grantee cannot obtain an allotment for personal cultivation when the allotment would enable eviction in breach of a grant condition protecting tenants from eviction.
material_facts: The grantee applied for allotment of land for personal cultivation under the legislation.
An allotment order would enable the grantee to evict tenants from the allotted land.
The grant was subject to a condition that the grantee would not evict the tenants, and that condition gave them a protected privilege.
The tribunals found that the tenants did not hold the special land rights that would exclude the land from the allotment provisions.
issues.conclusion: The application for allotment was incompetent because an order granting it would enable eviction in breach of the tenants’ protected privilege.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 19 and 20 of the Saurashtra Land Reforms Act, 1951, provide for applications and orders allotting land to a Girasdar for personal cultivation, with an allotment order enabling possession from a tenant. Section 18 prevents Chapter IV from limiting or abridging tenants’ rights or privileges arising from a grant. Section 27 excludes land where a tenant has acquired specified special rights; those rights were not found here. Accordingly, the Mamlatdar could not make an order enabling the grantee to evict the tenants in breach of the grant condition.

issues.definition: A personal-cultivation allotment application is incompetent when the resulting allotment would enable eviction contrary to a protected grant condition and the tenants do not hold special land rights that independently exclude the land from allotment.

issues.legal_issue: A notification declaring a grantee to be a Girasdar subject to tenant-protection provisions records the disability already imposed by the legislation rather than creating a new one.
material_facts: The government notified that the grantee was a Girasdar for the purposes of the legislation subject to its tenant-protection provision.
The government later clarified that the grantee remained subject to the condition against evicting the tenants.
The legislation itself preserved the tenants’ rights arising from the condition attached to the grant.
issues.conclusion: The notification stated the grantee’s existing disability under the legislation; it did not create a new restriction on his rights.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 2(15) of the Saurashtra Land Reforms Act, 1951, a person could be declared a Girasdar by notification. Section 18 preserved tenants’ rights and privileges arising from a grant. The declaration that the grantee was subject to section 18 therefore stated the consequence of the legislation, including the existing condition against eviction.

predicates.girasdar_notification_dispute: The dispute concerns a notification declaring a person to be a Girasdar subject to tenant-protection requirements.
predicates.notification_declares_status_subject_to_: The notification declares the grantee’s status subject to the requirements that protect tenants.
predicates.statute_preserves_existing_tenant_privil: The legislation preserves tenants’ privileges arising from an existing grant condition.
predicates.notification_records_existing_eviction_d: The notification records an existing restriction on the grantee’s ability to evict tenants rather than creating a new one.

issues.definition: When a notification declares a grantee’s status subject to tenant protection and the legislation already preserves the tenants’ grant-based privileges, the notification records the existing restriction on eviction.
